activities.anchor: etiquette of a language they cannot yet order coffee in
activities.caption: file each rule by its kind
activities.name: gwtRuleBuckets

config.prompt: Two meanings of "grammar" — file each rule under the one it belongs to:

items.label: what speakers of the language actually do — what the linguistics lessons formalised
"no split infinitives" — violated by "to boldly go", which is perfect English
usually eighteenth- and nineteenth-century inventions, often borrowed from Latin
politeness levels and formal endings — real facts about the language
learn this first; feel out the register rules once you can tell which situations they govern

config.why: Description records the real system; prescription is style-guide invention layered on top — and learners waste years polishing a system they cannot yet use.

activities.anchor: well over half of running discourse in chunks
activities.caption: find the line the paradigm-first mistake would love
activities.name: gwtChunkSpot

config.prompt: One line of this study plan is the classic self-taught error — click it:
lines: Fluent speech is largely formulaic — most of running talk is prefabricated.
Learn the load-bearing patterns as wholes; dissect the internal grammar later.
Chase the full conjugation table first — the chunks will assemble from it.
The paradigm is the reference document; the chunks are the acquisition vehicle.
A chunk learned whole is immediately fluent.
config.correction: Chunks first, tables afterward — that is the "patterns before paradigms" principle.
config.why: A chunk learned whole is immediately fluent, and the analysis has somewhere to land when it comes; the table swallowed first is cargo, not a map.

activities.anchor: Immersion is the diet; noticing is the digestion.
activities.caption: bet on what the ear skips
activities.name: gwtInputOnlyPredict

config.q: An input-only learner understands plenty but speaks in safe formulas. What keeps getting skipped?
choices: The low-salience marks that carry meaning — past-tense endings, articles
config.why: Unless attention is deliberately pointed at them, those marks keep sliding past — input supplies the evidence, focused study makes the pattern visible, output forces it into production.

activities.caption: line up the loop, notice first
activities.name: gwtLoopOrder

config.prompt: Schmidt's (1990) claim made noticing central — now order the loop this lesson installs:
items: Notice — a pattern starts recurring in your input hours
Study — five minutes on what it is called, with your collected examples in hand
Use — produce it deliberately for a week: self-talk, tutoring, writing
Next cycle — one pattern at a time, to felt mastery
config.why: Serial focus beats parallel confusion: twenty or thirty load-bearing structures, covered in the order that actually installs.

pairs.left: a week of narrating your day aloud

config.why: The rule was never the entry point; it was the sharpening stone.

activities.anchor: they map exactly what your current internal grammar believes
activities.caption: true or false — reading your own errors
activities.name: gwtErrorJudge

statements.s: Learner errors are systematic: they show what the current system believes.
statements.why: The developing system — interlanguage — is rule-building, not failure.

statements.s: Transient slips need nothing but input and time.
statements.why: The ones that change month to month fix themselves.
It teaches avoidance, not accuracy — feedback is best focused and delayed.

statements.s: Without a log, you fix what you already know how to fix.
statements.why: The guesses are systematically wrong — the log is the diagnostic instrument.

statements.s: Staged errors like native children's are evidence of failure.
statements.why: They are evidence of rule-building — the same stages, in the same order.

activities.anchor: a map, not swallowed beforehand as cargo
activities.caption: call the count — Finnish cases
activities.name: gwtFinnishEstimate

config.prompt: How many cases does Finnish have?
config.why: Fifteen — and they yield as fifteen recurring phrase-patterns, the way German gender arrives bundled in "der Mann", "die Frau", "das Kind" and the case system assembles itself from hundreds of witnessed instances.
config.context: The chunks are the acquisition vehicle; the table is consulted afterward.

activities.anchor: translation back is always harder than understanding
activities.caption: drag the divider — recognise, then own
activities.name: gwtFreeCompare

config.prompt: The gap this lesson exists to close — drag the divider:

before.label: Recognising
before.text: You parse it in the transcript — the pattern met, the meaning recovered.

after.label: Owning
after.text: You produce it — the chunk routes out of your mouth, not around; free translation's back-translation diffs show which is which.

config.why: The diffs are your interlanguage made visible — five sentences a week is enough, uncomfortable and disproportionately diagnostic.
